articles.title: The farmer who turned to singing after bovine TB silenced his fields
articles.summary: Dairy farmer Mervyn Kelso struggled with the sadness of the empty fields when he lost his entire herd to bovine TB.
articles.content:
When bovine TB led to the loss of his entire herd, dairy farmer Mervyn Kelso struggled with the sadness of the empty fields and the silence of the milking yard.

It was a traumatic time for a man who had farmed his whole life, and it was hard watching his neighbours tend to their cows.

His sister suggested he should join the Farmers' Choir and that turned out to be a "great lifter".

Fast forward four years, and Mervyn has sang for the King, met musical royalty and his choir is up for a national award.

Mervyn's first batch of cows were lost in November 2021. At the same time, a friend who had been around the County Antrim farm for three generations died.

Then another 120 cows had to be removed, followed by 40 more two months later.

"The department decided to buy the herd out," said Mervyn.

"So by March 2022 we had no stock, no milking stock or adult stock."

Mervyn and his wife Ruth, who live near Portglenone, relied on their faith for "the strength to carry on".

Mervyn would sing in church and so when the Farmers' Choir restarted in nearby Ballymena that autumn, he decided to give it a go.

He said it had been rewarding and different - a relief to the tough challenges of day-to-day farming.

"Farming is one very lonely job, even more lonely than it was a generation ago, because labour is so difficult to get," he said.

"And it's a very dangerous job, especially for a man who's working on his own.

"It has the effect of depressing you, and that's why being involved in such a thing as a choir or any social event outside farming is good for anyone."
articles.reasoning: The article highlights a meaningful personal recovery and community connection through music after a devastating agricultural loss, offering emotional uplift and hope. While the impact is more individual and community-focused rather than broad societal change, it clearly describes a positive transformation and mental health benefit for a farmer affected by bovine TB.
articles.personality_title: Farmer finds new hope through singing after losing herd to disease
articles.personality_presentation:
**Context** – Mervyn Kelso is a dairy farmer from County Antrim who lost his entire herd of cows because of bovine tuberculosis (TB), a disease that affects cattle. This happened between late 2021 and early 2022, leaving his fields empty and his daily work suddenly very quiet.

**What happened** – After losing all his cows, Mervyn felt very sad and isolated. His sister suggested he join the local Farmers' Choir in Ballymena. Mervyn started singing with the group in autumn 2022, which helped him cope with the tough times. Since then, he has performed for the King, met famous musicians, and his choir is now up for a national award.

**Impact** – Singing in the choir gave Mervyn a new sense of purpose and connection. Farming is often lonely and stressful, especially when working alone. Joining the choir helped Mervyn feel less isolated and brought joy back into his life. It also showed how social activities can support mental health for farmers facing difficult challenges.

**What's next step** – Mervyn and his choir will continue to perform and possibly win the national award. His story may encourage other farmers to find support through community groups and activities beyond farming.

**One-sentence takeaway** – After losing his herd to bovine TB, farmer Mervyn Kelso found comfort and new opportunities by joining a local choir, showing the power of community and music in tough times.
articles.personality_title_fr: Un agriculteur retrouve l'espoir grâce au chant après la perte de son troupeau
articles.personality_presentation_fr:
**Contexte** – Mervyn Kelso est un éleveur laitier du comté d'Antrim qui a perdu tout son troupeau à cause de la tuberculose bovine (TB), une maladie qui touche les bovins. Cela s'est passé entre fin 2021 et début 2022, laissant ses champs vides et son travail quotidien soudainement très calme.

**Ce qui s'est passé** – Après avoir perdu toutes ses vaches, Mervyn s'est senti très triste et isolé. Sa sœur lui a suggéré de rejoindre la Chorale des Agriculteurs locale à Ballymena. Mervyn a commencé à chanter avec le groupe à l'automne 2022, ce qui l'a aidé à surmonter ces moments difficiles. Depuis, il a chanté pour le Roi, rencontré des musiciens célèbres, et sa chorale est désormais en lice pour un prix national.

**Impact** – Chanter dans la chorale a donné à Mervyn un nouveau sens et une connexion sociale. L'agriculture est souvent solitaire et stressante, surtout quand on travaille seul. Rejoindre la chorale a aidé Mervyn à se sentir moins isolé et a ramené de la joie dans sa vie. Cela montre aussi comment les activités sociales peuvent soutenir la santé mentale des agriculteurs face aux difficultés.

**Prochaine étape** – Mervyn et sa chorale continueront à se produire et pourraient gagner le prix national. Son histoire peut encourager d'autres agriculteurs à chercher du soutien dans des groupes communautaires et des activités en dehors de l'agriculture.

**En résumé** – Après avoir perdu son troupeau à cause de la tuberculose bovine, l'agriculteur Mervyn Kelso a trouvé du réconfort et de nouvelles opportunités en rejoignant une chorale locale, montrant le pouvoir de la communauté et de la musique dans les moments difficiles.
articles.personality_title_es: Agricultor encuentra nueva esperanza cantando tras perder su ganado por enfermedad
articles.personality_presentation_es:
**Contexto** – Mervyn Kelso es un granjero lechero del condado de Antrim que perdió todo su rebaño debido a la tuberculosis bovina (TB), una enfermedad que afecta al ganado. Esto ocurrió entre finales de 2021 y principios de 2022, dejando sus campos vacíos y su trabajo diario muy tranquilo.

**Qué pasó** – Después de perder todas sus vacas, Mervyn se sintió muy triste y aislado. Su hermana le sugirió unirse al Coro de Agricultores local en Ballymena. Mervyn comenzó a cantar con el grupo en otoño de 2022, lo que le ayudó a superar esos momentos difíciles. Desde entonces, ha cantado para el Rey, conocido a músicos famosos y su coro está nominado para un premio nacional.

**Impacto** – Cantar en el coro le dio a Mervyn un nuevo sentido y conexión social. La agricultura suele ser un trabajo solitario y estresante, especialmente si se trabaja solo. Unirse al coro ayudó a Mervyn a sentirse menos aislado y devolvió la alegría a su vida. También demuestra cómo las actividades sociales pueden apoyar la salud mental de los agricultores en tiempos difíciles.

**Próximo paso** – Mervyn y su coro seguirán actuando y podrían ganar el premio nacional. Su historia puede animar a otros agricultores a buscar apoyo en grupos comunitarios y actividades fuera de la agricultura.

**Conclusión en una frase** – Tras perder su rebaño por tuberculosis bovina, el granjero Mervyn Kelso encontró consuelo y nuevas oportunidades al unirse a un coro local, mostrando el poder de la comunidad y la música en tiempos difíciles.
